sentences.text: This ancient fish reached a length of roughly 35 centimeters and shared many traits with today's lungfish.
Unlike modern relatives where certain fins merge, this species possessed distinct dorsal, tail, and anal fins.
Adam Sedgwick and Roderick Murchison formally named the genus in the year 1828.
It stands as one of the earliest lungfish species ever identified by scientists.
Taxonomically, the animal falls within the class Dipnoi.
It is further grouped into the family Dipteridae.
This freshwater lungfish inhabited waters across Europe and perhaps North America during the middle Devonian.
Its existence spanned the Eifelian through the Famennian stages, occurring between 393.47 and 358.86 million years ago.
Scientists question whether many species defined by isolated tooth plates from Europe and North America truly belong to this genus, given their fragmentary state.
